sources.entry: Mackup - Keep your application settings in sync (macOS/Linux).

summary.one_liner: Mackup backs up and syncs application configuration files across machines, using a cloud-synced folder such as Dropbox, on macOS and GNU/Linux.
summary.what_it_does: Mackup copies pure configuration files for a long list of supported applications and command-line tools into a Mackup folder that you choose, such as one in Dropbox, iCloud, or Google Drive. Its copy mode runs "mackup backup" to save settings and "mackup restore" to put them back on a new machine. A separate link mode moves config files into the Mackup folder and replaces the originals with symlinks, and "mackup link uninstall" reverses this. Commands can be limited to a single app by name, and "mackup list" shows supported apps. Users can add their own files or directories through a ~/.mackup directory.
use_cases: back up application settings before reinstalling macOS or Linux
sync dotfiles and app configs between multiple workstations
restore configuration on a fresh computer
keep config files in Dropbox, iCloud, or Google Drive
version-control dotfiles in a Git-synced folder
move personal config files like ~/.config entries into a sync folder
notable: Copy mode for backup and restore, plus a separate link mode that symlinks configs into a synced folder
Large built-in list of supported applications and developer tools
Per-application scoping for backup, restore, link, and uninstall commands
Custom sync of arbitrary files or directories via a ~/.mackup directory
Written in GPL-licensed code according to the README author notes
caveats: Link mode breaks preferences on macOS Sonoma (14) and later; the README recommends copy mode instead
The link strategy does not work correctly on macOS according to the usage section
Box is no longer supported because it ignores dotfiles
summary.license: GPL (named in the README as GPL; exact version not stated)
